Roland Banks, the Fed, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror series of Cthulhu Mythos publications. He made his first appearance in the 2009 expansion Innsmouth Horror.

page.overview:
Who is Roland Banks?

Roland Banks, the Fed, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror series of Cthulhu Mythos publications. He made his first appearance in the 2009 expansion Innsmouth Horror.

As can be gathered from Fantasy Flight's various flavour texts, Roland is known for being something of a stickler for the rules. On occasion, however, in extraordinary circumstances, he is shown to be willing to throw procedure out of the window in the interests of serving justice, as seen when he tackled the case of a murdered orchestra (see "History," below).

Banks had been a model agent for his entire career, but during one particular investigation had the bad luck to get caught up in a local situation in which corrupt local authorities had struck a deal with local bootleggers to supply their town with illegal hooch. Although Banks tried to bring the authorities to justice, it transpired that at least one of the perpetrators had had connections high in the federal bureaucracy. Immediately removed from the case, he was reassigned, and word went out within the bureau that Banks was now blacklisted.(: The Dirge of Reason)

Banks was subsequently assigned to investigate a case in the jurisdiction of Arkham, the case of a murdered orchestra which the Bureau had been pressured to solve by yet more meddling higher-ups, and which his superiors believed would be unsolvable - adding yet another black mark to his record. As it turned out, Banks was far more resourceful and open-minded than his superiors had counted on, and discovered that the orchestra's conductor had been putting ancient Sumerian texts to music, accidentally summoning an otherworldly entity which destroyed them all. Banks managed to defeat the being and close the gate torn open by the orchestra's music, and file a report which seemed plausible yet contained no mention of the supernatural causes which would have had him labelled as a kook.(: The Dirge of Reason)
